Chemotherapy
for Dogs and Cats
Chemotherapy for dogs and cats is very different from treatment in humans. Our dosages and dose frequency are carefully modified to maintain a good quality of life both during and after treatment. A course of treatment is not continued unless it provides both adequate control of disease and a good day-to-day quality of life. Only about 20–30% of patients develop side effects that impact their quality of life. When side effects do occur, they typically resolve within a few days and can be readily controlled with oral medications at home.
How Chemotherapy Is Used
Chemotherapy can be used as a sole treatment for many cancers of the immune system, especially lymphoma and leukemia. For solid tumors, chemotherapy is generally directed at treating microscopic amounts of cancer to help prevent the development of visible metastasis. It is often combined with other treatments, such as surgery or radiation therapy, to address visible cancer lesions.
What to Expect at Our Hospital
Most chemotherapy treatments are given in our hospital as injections or oral medications. Side effects are generally mild and temporary.
You will receive detailed written discharges and clear instructions on what to watch for at home. Our goal is for pets to continue to eat, play, and enjoy their daily routines throughout treatment.
